content.title: Is ‘The Bachelorette’ really canceled? What ABC has said about Taylor Frankie Paul’s season
content.text: If you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.The future of “The Bachelorette” is unclear, as ABC decided to pull the new season, which was slated to premiere this Sunday.Why did ABC pull ‘The Bachelorette’ before its Sunday premiere?Led by reality star Taylor Frankie Paul, Season 22 will no longer make its debut following confirmation from a spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department of a domestic assault investigation involving “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star and her ex, Dakota Mortensen, as well as a 2023 video recently uncovered by TMZ showing a separate alleged assault on Dakota, for which Taylor later entered a plea deal in abeyance on an aggravated assault charge and was placed on three years’ probation, ending in August.“In light of the newly released video that just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of ‘The Bachelorette’ at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family,” a Disney Entertainment Television spokesperson said in a statement.In response to the 2023 video, a rep for Taylor shared with TMZ: “It’s sad to see the latest installment of his never-ending, desperate, attention-seeking, destructive campaign to harm Taylor without any regard for the consequences for their child. Releasing an old and selectively edited video on their son’s birthday is a reprehensible attempt to distract from his own behavior.” They added, “Thankfully, the public has seen this act before and knows who he is and sadly, many will recognize this pattern of manipulation, both in his actions on the show and from their own experiences.”She also responded to the decision to pull “The Bachelorette” season. A spokesperson for Paul stated in a message to People, “Taylor is very grateful for ABC’s support as she prioritizes her family’s safety and security. After years of silently suffering extensive mental and physical abuse as well as threats of retaliation, Taylor is finally gaining the strength to face her accuser and taking steps to ensure that she and her children are protected from any further harm.”The statement continued, “There are too many women who are suffering in silence as they survive aggressive, jealous ex-partners who refuse to let them move on with their lives. Taylor has remained silent out of fear of further abuse, retaliation and public shaming. She is currently exploring all of her options, seeking support, and preparing to own and share her story.”The 2023 domestic incident was publicly known prior to her being cast on “The Bachelorette,” and was even featured in Season 1 of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.”Taylor and Dakota have one son together, age 2, and she shares two children with ex-husband Tate Paul, age 8 and 5.NEW YORK, NEW YORK - FEBRUARY 2: (EXCLUSIVE COVERAGE) Whitney Leavitt poses backstage with her "The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" cast at "Chicago" on Broadway at The Ambassador Theatre on February 2, 2026 in New York City.Bruce Glikas/Getty ImagesHow ‘The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ has reactedLess than a week following the Season 4 premiere on Hulu, filming for Season 5 of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” has also been halted amid the recent domestic assault investigation. It’s unclear whose decision it was to pause production, but one star from the show, Mikayla Matthews, spoke out on Thursday, sharing in an “AMA” on her Instagram story, “It was a decision that all us girls came up with and agreed on. We didn’t feel comfortable filming with everything that was happening.”Sources also shared with People that “none of the women want to be associated with [Taylor].”According to audio from a March 7 Zoom meeting between the cast and ABC executives obtained by NBC News, the cast has raised safety concerns about promoting and continuing the show as long as Taylor is involved. Is ‘The Bachelorette’ canceled, or could it still air later?Despite the uncertainty surrounding Taylor’s season of “The Bachelorette,” there are signs it may not be permanently shelved. Promotional material remains visible across ABC’s social media platforms. That continued visibility, along with the financial loss of at least $2 million in production costs per episode, has fueled speculation that the season could be delayed and eventually air.Taylor’s “Before the First Rose” special is still available to stream on Hulu and Fubo. Seasons 1–4 of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” can also be streamed on demand on Hulu.“The Bachelorette” Season 22 was originally supposed to air Sundays on ABC, starting March 22. In place of the season premiere, ABC will air a rerun of “American Idol” Season 24, Episode 8.
